outcomes: Explain why an f32 performance kernel needs tolerance-based comparison with an f64 numerical oracle
Construct a release-mode benchmark with warmups and repeated samples
Report latency with units, variability, work, and measured throughput
Calculate and qualify an arithmetic-intensity estimate
Use profiling evidence to choose a useful optimization target

floating-point.name: Floating point
floating-point.definition: A finite binary representation of numbers across a wide range of magnitudes.
floating-point.explanation: Rust f32 follows IEEE-754 binary32 arithmetic for ordinary values. Most real numbers are not exactly representable, so operations round. Addition is therefore not mathematically associative: changing reduction order can alter low bits. Fused multiply-add performs a multiplication and addition with one final rounding. Optimized kernels preserve the numerical method, but comparisons should use a documented absolute-plus-relative tolerance unless a fixed environment and exact operation order are explicit requirements.

benchmark.name: Benchmark
benchmark.definition: A controlled experiment measuring a specified workload under recorded conditions.
benchmark.explanation: A useful benchmark identifies its input shapes, data type, build mode, machine, timed boundary, warmups, repetitions, and statistic. It also checks that the computation remains correct and makes its output observable. Kernel timing excludes setup such as allocation and printing; end-to-end timing includes those costs and answers another question. A benchmark result is evidence for that workload and environment, not a universal speed claim.

throughput.name: Throughput
throughput.definition: The amount of useful work completed per unit of elapsed time.
throughput.explanation: For dense matrix work, throughput is often reported as billions of floating-point operations per second, or GFLOP/s. The numerator comes from a stated algorithmic counting convention, while the denominator is measured time. Throughput helps compare sizes with different operation counts, but it must remain beside latency, dimensions, precision, and hardware. A high rate does not establish correctness or model quality, and differing operation conventions can make apparently similar rates incomparable.

arithmetic-intensity.name: Arithmetic intensity
arithmetic-intensity.definition: Useful arithmetic operations divided by bytes transferred across a named memory boundary.
arithmetic-intensity.explanation: Arithmetic intensity connects an algorithm’s work with data movement. A dense layer can reuse weights across batch rows, raising intensity, while a streaming elementwise operation usually performs little work per byte. The memory boundary must be stated: DRAM-to-cache traffic differs from cache-to-register traffic. Counting each array once gives a cold-array traffic estimate; warmed calls may already have those arrays cached, so this is not a DRAM lower bound. Hardware counters and profiling are needed before claiming which memory level limits a real run.

Benchmark reports unit-bearing median and range values, checksum, GFLOP/s, cold-array traffic estimate, and estimated FLOP/byte
